walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: stages, parts and storage

steps.text: A similar question. A washing machine has three stages: wash, rinse and spin. One stage is spin. Identify one other stage.
The question gives one stage. Any one of the other two earns the mark. Never give back the stage the question names.
steps.visual: given: spin → answer: wash or rinse

steps.text: Your part (a): the CPU cycle has three stages, in order. The last one is given. Name one of the two that come before it.
A similar question. Which part of the CPU sends signals to manage the cycle? Ask: which part is in charge?
steps.visual: in charge, sends signals: the control unit

steps.text: Your part (b): ask a different question. Which part does the working out: adding, comparing, true or false?

Your part (c): primary storage has two kinds. One keeps the start-up instructions and cannot be changed. The other holds the programs and data in use now. Which one does the CPU take each instruction from?
steps.visual:
read only memory: start-up instructions
?: programs and data in use now

steps.label: Do Now: Registers (2 of 2)
steps.content:
Do Now: Registers (2 of 2)

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does a "State the purpose" question want what a part is for, not where it is?Show the answer

The mark is for its job. Saying where a part is, or what it looks like, does not show what it does.

Part (a): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, June 2026, Question 2(a)(i). A smartphone has a quad-core 2.4 GHz processor. The processor performs the fetch-decode-execute (FDE) cycle. Part (b): Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2024, Question 8(b)(i). The CPU contains registers.

Total: 2 marks

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: the first register and a register

steps.text: The cycle starts with fetch. Before the CPU can fetch, it must know where the next instruction is in RAM.
steps.visual: a place in RAM is called an address

steps.text: So the first register holds an address: the address of the next instruction.
steps.visual:
RAM address 4: LOAD 7
RAM address 5: ADD 8

steps.text: Your part (a): which register keeps the address of the next instruction, and adds 1 after each fetch? Its name says that it counts.
A similar question. State the purpose of a bus. Say what it does, with what.
steps.visual: A bus carries values between components.

steps.text: A register is a different kind of part. It is a tiny store inside the CPU, very close to the ALU and the CU.
steps.visual: inside the CPU, next to the parts that use it

steps.text: Your part (b): what does a register hold? And for how long: for ever, or only while the CPU works on it?
steps.visual: what it holds + for how long

steps.label: The CPU and the FDE Cycle Exam Practice
steps.content:
3.1 Review: Exam Practice 1

The CPU and the FDE Cycle

Year 10

  • Today: real exam questions on the parts of the CPU, the registers, the buses and the FDE cycle.
  • Also: a practice paper, and fix answers that lose marks.
Think → Pair → ShareAn exam question has 3 marks. Why is one long sentence about one idea not enough?Show the answer

Each mark is for a different point. One idea, said in many ways, still gets one mark.

steps.label: Key Facts: The CPU
steps.content:
Key Facts: The CPU

  • CPU: processes instructions and data.
  • ALU: does calculations and logic. CU: decodes instructions and sends signals.
  • PC: holds the address of the next instruction.
  • MAR: holds the address to read or write. MDR: holds the data or instruction read or to write.
  • CIR: holds the instruction being decoded and executed. ACC: holds the result of a calculation.
  • Address bus: carries addresses, one way. Data bus: carries data, both ways. Control bus: carries signals, both ways.
  • Fetch: PC to MAR, PC goes up by 1, the instruction goes to the MDR, then to the CIR. Decode: the CU decodes it. Execute: it is carried out.
Think → Pair → ShareWhich of these facts do you find hardest to remember?Show the answer

Everyone has a different answer. Copy that fact into your notes now.

steps.label: The CPU: The Accumulator
steps.content:
The CPU: The Accumulator

Think → Pair → ShareThis question asks two things. Why plan where each mark will come from?Show the answer

One mark is for naming the part and two are for the purpose. A plan stops you writing three points about only one of them.

4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2022, Question 2(c). Phil has a computer that is designed using the Von Neumann model. The computer has a central processing unit (CPU).

items.prompt: Identify the component within the CPU that the accumulator is built into and describe the purpose of the accumulator.
items.modelAnswer: It is built into the ALU. It temporarily stores data. It stores the results of calculations.
scheme: the component: arithmetic logic unit / ALU
it stores the result of interim calculations
items.context: 4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2022, Question 2(c). Phil has a computer that is designed using the Von Neumann model. The computer has a central processing unit (CPU). Question: Identify the component within the CPU that the accumulator is built into and describe the purpose of the accumulator. Marking rule: One mark for the component (ALU), then any two from, one mark for each point met, up to 3.

steps.label: Von Neumann: Fix the Answer
steps.content:
Von Neumann: Fix the Answer

Think → Pair → ShareWhy can an answer that sounds right still get 0 marks?Show the answer

It may only say the question again in other words. A mark needs a fact the question did not already give.

4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2021, Question 8(a). The Von Neumann model, for a computer system, uses the stored program concept. Describe what is meant by the stored program concept.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: “The program is stored on the computer so it can be used again later.”
This answer gets 0 marks. Write a better answer that gets 2 marks.
items.modelAnswer: Instructions and data are stored in the same memory. Instructions are fetched and executed in order.
scheme: instructions and data stored in the same / main memory
instructions fetched and executed in order / one after another / in sequence
items.ariaLabel: Describe what is meant by the stored program concept. (better answer)
items.context: 4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2021, Question 8(a). The Von Neumann model, for a computer system, uses the stored program concept. Describe what is meant by the stored program concept. A student wrote: "The program is stored on the computer so it can be used again later." This got 0 of 2 marks: it does not say where the instructions and data are kept, or how the instructions are run. The student now writes a better answer. Marking rule: One mark each, one mark for each point met, up to 2.

steps.label: Buses: One Bus and Its Purpose
steps.content:
Buses: One Bus and Its Purpose

Think → Pair → ShareWhy must the purpose match the bus you named?Show the answer

Each bus carries one kind of value. A purpose that belongs to a different bus earns nothing.

4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2023, Question 2(c)(ii). A library has a self-checkout system that allows customers to register books that they want to borrow. The self-checkout system has a central processing unit (CPU). The CPU contains registers and buses.

items.prompt: Identify one bus that can be found in the CPU and explain its purpose in the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
items.modelAnswer: Data bus. It carries data between components in the CPU.
scheme: address bus / data bus / control bus (one mark for the name)
address bus: transmits / carries addresses ... between components in the CPU
data bus: transmits / carries data ... between components in the CPU
control bus: transmits control signals ... from the control unit to other components in the CPU
items.context: 4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2023, Question 2(c)(ii). A library has a self-checkout system that allows customers to register books that they want to borrow. The self-checkout system has a central processing unit (CPU). The CPU contains registers and buses. Question: Identify one bus that can be found in the CPU and explain its purpose in the fetch-decode-execute cycle. Marking rule: One mark for the bus, two marks for the matching description, one mark for each point met, up to 3.

steps.label: Registers: Fix the Answer
steps.content:
Registers: Fix the Answer

Think → Pair → ShareTwo registers have names that look alike. How can you remember which holds what?Show the answer

Read the middle word of each name. It says what kind of value that register holds.

4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 2(c). A computer has a central processing unit (CPU). A value is fetched from random access memory (RAM) to the CPU. Explain how the MAR and MDR are used in this process.

items.prompt:
A student wrote: “The MDR holds the address of the value, and the MAR holds the value when it arrives from RAM.”
This answer gets 0 marks. Write a better answer that gets 3 marks.
items.modelAnswer: The MAR holds the address of the value to be fetched. The value is copied into the MDR.
scheme: the MAR stores / holds the address / location // the address is sent / copied to the MAR ...
... for the value / data that is to be fetched / in RAM
the MDR stores / holds the value / data // the data is sent / copied to the MDR
items.ariaLabel: Explain how the MAR and MDR are used in this process. (better answer)
items.context: 4 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, June 2026, Question 2(c). A computer has a central processing unit (CPU). A value is fetched from random access memory (RAM) to the CPU. Explain how the MAR and MDR are used in this process. A student wrote: "The MDR holds the address of the value, and the MAR holds the value when it arrives from RAM." This got 0 of 3 marks: the two registers are swapped: the MAR holds the address and the MDR holds the value. The student now writes a better answer. Marking rule: Three from, one mark for each point met, up to 3.

steps.label: The FDE Cycle: The Program Counter
steps.content:
The FDE Cycle: The Program Counter

Think → Pair → ShareA register holds one value. Why does the exam want you to say which value?Show the answer

Every register holds a value. Saying which one shows what makes this register different.

3 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2021, Question 8(b)(i). The fetch-execute cycle of a Von Neumann model, for a computer system, uses registers and buses.

items.prompt: Describe the role of the Program Counter.
items.modelAnswer: It holds the address of the next instruction.
items.context: 3 minutes. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2021, Question 8(b)(i). The fetch-execute cycle of a Von Neumann model, for a computer system, uses registers and buses. Question: Describe the role of the Program Counter. Marking rule: One mark each, one mark for each point met, up to 2.
